child: Write {member} a note telling them one thing you like about them.
adult: Write {member} a note about something you appreciate in them but haven't said.

child: Write {member} a note: 'I feel happy when you…'
adult: Write {member} a note that finishes: 'I feel close to you when…'

child: Write {member} a 'thank you' note for something they did this week.
adult: Write {member} a thank-you note for something specific they did recently.

child: Write {member} a note about a favourite memory you have together.
adult: Write {member} about a memory with them that you treasure.

child: Hide a kind note somewhere {member} will find it.
adult: Leave a surprise note for {member} – in their bag, lunchbox or on the mirror.

child: Make a 'feelings signal' with {member}: a thumbs up means 'I'm OK', a wave means 'I need a hug'.
adult: Agree on a simple signal with {member} for 'I need space' and 'I need you'.

child: Start a shared notebook with {member}. Write one line and give it to them.
adult: Start a shared notebook with {member}: write a few lines and pass it to them.

child: Write {member} a note: 'Something I wish you knew about me is…'
adult: Write {member} a note that starts: 'Something I wish you knew about me is…'

child: Write {member} a list of 3 things they do that make you happy.
adult: Write {member} a list of small, everyday things they do that you're grateful for.

child: Write {member} a note about a time they made you proud.
adult: Write {member} about a moment you were proud of them – say exactly what they did.

child: Write {member} a note asking for help with something that's hard for you.
adult: Write {member} about something you'd like their help with, and how you'd like them to help.

child: Make a 'question jar' with {member}: each write 3 questions and answer one together.
adult: Make a question jar with {member}. Each add three questions, then answer one together tonight.

child: Send {member} a voice note saying something nice.
adult: Send {member} a voice note telling them what they mean to you.

child: Make {member} a card for no reason at all.
adult: Make or buy {member} a card for no special reason, and write something real in it.

child: Send {member} a message using only emojis. Ask them to guess what it means!
adult: Send {member} a song that says something you'd struggle to put into words.

child: Write {member} a note: 'One thing I'd like us to do more is…'
adult: Write {member} a note: 'One thing I'd love us to do more of is…'

child: Tell {member} 'good night' with a special message every night for 3 nights.
adult: Send {member} a short message each day for three days – a thought, a memory, a 'thinking of you'.

child: Write {member} a note about what makes your family special.
adult: Write {member} a letter to be opened in one year. Hand it over sealed.

child: Ask {member} 3 questions about their day and really listen to the answers.
adult: Ask {member} three questions about their day and listen without your phone.

child: Write {member} a note about something you'd like to do together this weekend.
adult: Write {member} an invitation to something you'd like to do together this week.
